blogs.title: From 16‑bit to 1.58‑bit: The Quantum Leap in Large Language Model Efficiency
blogs.description: An introductory post that explains why researchers are pushing quantization beyond traditional 4‑bit methods, walks through the evolution from FP16/BF16 to 1‑bit models, and sets the stage for why BitNet b1.58 matters for both performance and sustainability.

blogs.title: Inside BitNet b1.58: How Ternary Weights Turn a Full‑Precision Model Light
blogs.-description: A deep dive into the architecture of BitNet b1.58—covering the BitLinear layer, the abs‑mean quantization function that forces weights into {‑1, 0, +1}, the use of RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings, and how these pieces plug into existing LLaMA‑style codebases.

blogs.title: Benchmarking the Unthinkable: A 3B Ternary LLM Matches FP16 on Perplexity and Tasks
blogs.-description: A results‑focused article that walks readers through the experimental setup (RedPajama data, 100 B tokens), compares perplexity and zero‑shot scores across ARC®, Hellaswag®, Winogrande®, PIQA®, etc., and explains the new scaling law that lets a 13B bit‑model beat a 3B FP16 model in latency, memory, and energy.

blogs.title: Energy Savings at Scale: Why 1‑bit LLMs Are a Game‑Changer for Green AI
blogs.-description: Explores the energy model behind BitNet b1.58, showing how replacing FP16 multiplies with integer additions reduces arithmetic energy by over 70× on modern silicon, illustrates real‑world power draw estimates for models up to 70 B parameters, and discusses the environmental impact of deploying such models.

blogs.title: Running AI on Your Phone: Bringing Large Language Models to Edge with BitNet
blogs.-description: Translates the technical benefits of ternary weights into practical advantages for mobile and edge devices—smaller memory footprints enable longer context windows, higher throughput on CPUs/NPUs, and opens up new app scenarios previously impossible with FP16 models.

blogs.title: Designing the Next Generation of AI Chips for 1‑bit LLMs
blogs.-description: Looks ahead at hardware implications—what an accelerator optimized for ternary matrix multiplication might look like, lessons from Groq’s LPUs, architectural tweaks (e.g., on‑chip SRAM sizing, INT8 addition pipelines), and how hardware–software co‑design can unlock further speedups.

blogs.title: Getting Started with BitNet b1.58: A Hands‑On Tutorial Using Hugging Face & llama.cpp
blogs.-description: A step‑by‑step guide for practitioners—how to download a pretrained BitNet b1.58 checkpoint, load it in Hugging Face Transformers or llama.cpp, run inference on a GPU or CPU, fine‑tune on a downstream task, and benchmark latency/memory yourself.
